# Eval Infrastructure for Agent Systems

> A field guide to building production-grade evaluation infrastructure for LLM agent systems. Based on real production work at Airbnb (BPI Virtual Analyst), Shell (NLP classification), and contributions to LangChain, LiveKit, and Ragas.
> Source: https://github.com/sailikhithk/eval-infra-for-agents

Most LLM agent evaluation is ad hoc. Teams ship agents to production with manual spot-checks, vibe-based quality assessments, and no systematic way to detect regressions when prompts, models, or retrieval pipelines change. This handbook is a field guide for ML engineers who need to build real evaluation infrastructure: the kind that runs 23+ agent versions against 1,690 versioned ground-truth samples, detects regressions before they reach production, and gives the team confidence to ship.

## What you will learn

- How to build a reproducible evaluation harness that runs multiple agent versions against versioned ground-truth samples
- How to design dual-model A/B comparison and flip-analysis to detect regressions
- How to orchestrate 30+ LLM integrations behind a unified abstraction (FacadeDriver pattern)
- How to implement PII-safe batching and streaming pipelines for eval at scale
- How to track LLM costs accurately across providers (the gap that LangChain PR #39351 fixed)
- How to score agent reliability after a call ends (the LiveKit ReliabilityObserver pattern)
- How to build a culture of test-first agent development

## Chapters

- [Chapter 1: The Eval Problem](chapters/01-the-eval-problem.md) - Why ad hoc eval fails at scale
- [Chapter 2: Ground Truth](chapters/02-ground-truth.md) - Building a versioned sample store with PII redaction (1,690 samples)
- [Chapter 3: The FacadeDriver Pattern](chapters/03-facadedriver.md) - Multi-LLM orchestration (30+ models behind one interface)
- Chapter 4: Dual-Model A/B and Flip Analysis (planned)
- Chapter 5: Cost Tracking at Scale (planned)
- Chapter 6: Reliability Scoring After Call End (planned)
- Chapter 7: PII-Safe Batching and Streaming (planned)
- Chapter 8: Scaling from 600 to 10,000 Rows Per Run (planned)

- Chapter 10: Open-Source Eval Tools (planned)

## Notebooks

- [facadedriver_abstraction.ipynb](notebooks/facadedriver_abstraction.ipynb) - Interactive FacadeDriver pattern walkthrough

## Production numbers

- 23+ agent versions tracked
- 1,690 versioned ground-truth samples
- 30+ LLM integrations behind FacadeDriver
- 128+ users across 4 teams at Airbnb
- F1 0.654 (project-best)
- LLM-as-Judge gate: precision < 0.85 blocks production
- Scaled from 600 to 10,000 rows per run (40MB uploads, PII-safe)
